idiom_name: pest::pratt_parser::PrattParser (or chumsky::pratt) over the grammar's pair stream
implementation_notes: Rust has first-class Pratt support in its parsing libraries: pest's PrattParser declares precedence through the order of .op(Op::infix(rule, Assoc::Left) | ...) calls and consumes the pair stream a pest grammar produces, with map_primary/map_prefix/map_postfix/map_infix supplying the semantics and parse() running the loop; chumsky's pratt module offers the same idea inside a combinator parser. Because the grammar owns tokenisation you never write the nud/led table yourself, and the library's contract - pairs must alternate prefix* ~ primary ~ postfix* ~ (infix ~ prefix* ~ primary ~ postfix*)* - turns malformed grammars into immediate, positioned failures instead of wrong trees. Hand-rolling the climbing loop remains reasonable when the parser must be dependency-free or share state with a custom lexer (rustc's own parser climbs precedence by hand), but for a Rust-hosted DSL the library route removes the whole class of binding-power bugs.
code_sketch:
let pratt = PrattParser::<Rule>::new()
    .op(Op::infix(Rule::add, Assoc::Left) | Op::infix(Rule::sub, Assoc::Left))
    .op(Op::infix(Rule::mul, Assoc::Left))
    .op(Op::prefix(Rule::neg));
pratt
    .map_primary(|p| Expr::Lit(p.as_str().parse().unwrap()))
    .map_prefix(|op, rhs| Expr::Neg(Box::new(rhs)))
    .map_infix(|lhs, op, rhs| Expr::Binary { op: op.as_rule(), lhs: Box::new(lhs), rhs: Box::new(rhs) })
    .parse(pairs)
pitfalls: The pair stream must alternate exactly as the contract requires; a grammar that flattens it differently, or an empty input, causes a panic rather than a ParseError, so the grammar shape belongs in tests.
Precedence is the call order of op(): reordering builder calls silently changes both precedence and associativity for every operator in the ladder.
Every operator kind the grammar can produce needs its map_* closure, or the parser panics mid-parse; keep the Rule enum and the builder list in sync and match all variants in each closure.
